name: Pipedream
tagline: Run a small event-triggered code workflow with approved credentials and durable logs

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Hard daily credit cap plus active-workflow and connected-account caps; current numeric values are not exposed on the public pricing page.
tiers.notes: Connect is free only in development mode.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.notes: Prices and included credits are corroborated in official Pipedream support content; the live pricing application did not render its numeric cards.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: 2,000 included credits/month; unlimited workflows; 5 connected accounts; up to 10 GB RAM, 750-second runs and 30-day history.
tiers.notes: Prices are monthly and annual-effective figures corroborated in official support content.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 5,000 included credits/month; higher collaboration and governance limits; exact live platform fee not publicly rendered.

tiers.name: Connect
tiers.limits: 10,000 included credits/month and 100 active external users; $2 per additional active external user.
tiers.notes: Official support states $99/month on an annual commitment; monthly price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom credits, users, security, support and contract terms.

pricing.freeTierCaps: a permanent free plan exists, but its current daily credit, active-workflow and connected-account numbers were not exposed by the live public pricing page
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual on selected paid plans; platform fee is charged at the start of each cycle and usage overage with the next invoice
pricing.hiddenCosts: Workflows use 1 credit per 30 seconds at 256 MB per execution segment, multiplied by memory. Paid plans have no hard credit cap unless the customer sets one; additional credits are billed after the included amount. Connect also charges $2 per active external user above 100.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Pipedream, run a small event-triggered code workflow with approved credentials and durable logs. The hard boundary is managed runtime, event sources, oauth, secrets, connectors, scale, and support, plus connector breadth and execution reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Connect two specific services with a small event-triggered code workflow, use approved credentials, expose retries and durable logs, and avoid claiming a general integration platform.
requirements: OAuth or API credentials for two chosen services
whatYouLose: managed runtime, event sources, OAuth, secrets, connectors, scale, and support
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, token refresh, webhooks, polling, schemas, retries, idempotency, queues, secrets, rate limits, observability, and upgrades
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Pipedream because one automation is easy; maintaining hundreds of connectors and making every run recoverable is the business. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, token refresh, webhooks, polling, schemas, retries, idempotency, queues, secrets, rate limits, observability, and upgrades, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Activepieces
priorArt.desc: Active open-source automation platform with connectors and durable workflow execution.

alternatives.name: Kestra Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Event-triggered code, schedules, retries, logs, and a workflow engine built for keeping receipts.

facts.install: Kestra Cloud signup or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: Workflow definitions and execution state in PostgreSQL; task outputs and artifacts in Kestra internal storage on a Docker volume, filesystem, or configured object store
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a heavier orchestration platform with more infrastructure concepts and fewer instant consumer-SaaS actions than Pipedream's quick hosted trigger-plus-code workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, PostgreSQL and persistent storage; production webhooks also require a public URL, TLS, secrets, backups, and plugin/runtime configuration

alternatives.name: n8n Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Code nodes, credentials, webhooks, retries, and execution logs in a self-hosted visual shell.

facts.install: Official Docker image or Docker Compose; SQLite by default, PostgreSQL optional
facts.dataFormat: Workflows, credentials, users, and execution history in SQLite or PostgreSQL; the persistent .n8n directory also holds the credential-encryption key and instance settings
facts.gapVsPaid: It has a broad visual automation catalog, but the self-hosted edition shifts uptime and upgrades to you and is less developer-centric than Pipedream's hosted code steps, logs and managed credentials.
facts.setupBlocker: A durable deployment needs Docker, a persistent volume and encryption key, plus a public domain, reverse-proxy TLS, webhook URL, backups, and credential/OAuth setup

alternatives.name: Windmill Community Edition
alternatives.desc: Pipedream with your own Postgres and no pretence that code has disappeared.

facts.install: Windmill Cloud signup or the Community Edition Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Scripts, flows, resources, encrypted secrets, job queue, results, and execution state in PostgreSQL; optional object storage holds large files, logs, and dependency caches
facts.gapVsPaid: It is optimized for scripts, internal tools and worker infrastructure, so small consumer-SaaS event workflows usually take more setup and have fewer ready-made triggers than Pipedream.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting starts several containers and PostgreSQL; you must change the default admin password and configure a base URL, TLS, OAuth/SMTP, backups, and worker runtimes

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a two-service personal automation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Pipedream in an empty repository.
Use TypeScript, Node.js 22, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect two specific services with a small event-triggered code workflow, use approved credentials, expose retries and durable logs, and avoid claiming a general integration platform.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement a fixed trigger, transform, condition, and action workflow model rather than a general visual language.
Connect exactly two named services using documented APIs and encrypted credentials.
Store every run, step input hash, output summary, retry, and final status in PostgreSQL.
Make side effects idempotent and support retry from the failed step without repeating completed actions.
Add rate limits, backoff, dead-letter handling, manual replay, cancellation, and secret rotation.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, sample workflows, tests, backups, and connector-limit documentation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a broad connector marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unreviewed user code execution.
Deliberately leave out enterprise governance, guaranteed execution, and vendor-operated OAuth apps.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
